overview: A separate rate-limiter tier sits in front of services and keeps a sliding window counter (current + previous window weighted) in Redis using atomic INCR with EXPIRE.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative fleet: 20 gateway instances, shared limit 100 requests/s/subject.
estimation.result: One coordinated state key enforces the intended global quota.
estimation.implication: Shard by subject/policy, use atomic scripts and account for hot-subject contention.

components.purpose: Mobile caller with intermittent connectivity for rate limiter.
components.rationale: Use stable request IDs and reconnect/cursor recovery rather than assuming one continuous session.

components.purpose: Distribute incoming connections across healthy instances for rate limiter.
components.rationale: Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing.

components.purpose: Sliding window counter; returns 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining
components.rationale: Share per-subject state and update atomically; define 429/retry responses and outage behavior.
Specify TTL and update strategy; durable state remains elsewhere unless an atomic admission decision explicitly depends on this store.

components.purpose: Implement the owned APIs and coordinate state transitions for rate limiter.
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

accessPatterns: Check and consume quota atomically on every protected request.
constraints: Use one Lua transaction for read/compute/write/expiry; hash-tag keys that must be updated together.

apiDetails.purpose: Decide whether one request may reach the backend.
apiDetails.rationale: Gateway middleware may invoke this internally; the separate limiter variant exposes the same internal contract. Define whether retries consume quota again.

apiDetails.purpose: Example backend endpoint protected by the limiter.
apiDetails.rationale: The backend executes only after the admission decision; use a coarse emergency local cap during shared-store outages.

buildSteps.title: Clients
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Mobile Client and name it “Clients”. Place it in the leftmost caller/background lane. Mobile caller with intermittent connectivity for rate limiter. Use stable request IDs and reconnect/cursor recovery rather than assuming one continuous session. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: LB
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Load Balancer and name it “LB”. Place it in column 2, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Clients. Distribute incoming connections across healthy instances for rate limiter. Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Rate Limiter
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Rate Limiter and name it “Rate Limiter”. Place it in column 3, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are LB. Sliding window counter; returns 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining Share per-subject state and update atomically; define 429/retry responses and outage behavior. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Redis
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Cache and name it “Redis”. Place it in column 4, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Rate Limiter. INCR + EXPIRE per window key (atomic) Specify TTL and update strategy; durable state remains elsewhere unless an atomic admission decision explicitly depends on this store. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Services
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Service and name it “Services”. Place it in column 4, row 2 of the HLD; its callers are Rate Limiter. Implement the owned APIs and coordinate state transitions for rate limiter. Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

steps.title: Clients → LB → Rate Limiter → Redis
steps.explanation: Atomically read previous/current windows, compute weighted usage, increment and set expiry.

steps.title: Rate Limiter → Services
steps.explanation: Forward only on an allow decision; a denial returns 429 plus retry information.

steps.title: Rate Limiter → Redis
steps.explanation: Bound the decision timeout and apply the documented fail-open/closed policy; do not multiply the quota across independent process counters.

failureCases.scenario: The shared counter store is unreachable
failureCases.handling: Choose fail-open for availability-oriented reads with a local emergency cap; fail-closed for expensive or sensitive operations. Bound the decision timeout and return a documented retry response.

alternatives: Use gateway token buckets for burst allowance and fewer hops. Use a dedicated sliding-window limiter for centralized policy and smoother quotas, accepting another decision hop. Define outage behavior per endpoint.
